title: Writing back a record field
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ Boolean work tapes, let $\mathrm{upd}:T\times\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\to T$, and let $\mathrm{seek}$ be a two-tape Boolean machine with state set $S$ and designated states $\mathrm{start},\mathrm{finish}$. Let $d$ be a four-tape configuration over the record alphabet, and let $f_s$ be a list of fields whose length is $k+3$ and which are stored on tape $0$ of $d$ in the sense that the record-tape contents agree with the joined fields at every specified offset. For any recording data, there is a time $t\le 4(k+2)(L+1)$, where $L$ is the length of the joined fields, such that the recording machine runs from the snapshot at the beginning of the backward write pass, with the designated field offset and empty auxiliary buffers, to the snapshot in its true-verdict state. Before the final step it visits neither the true nor false verdict state, and all work-tape heads remain within distance $L+1$ of their initial positions.
hypotheses_covered: $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $Q,T,S$ are types with decidable equality
